$comment: DEALER BRAND FILE. The only file you edit to rebrand the whole campaign. Run `npm run build` after editing.
$status: Colors and type lockup derived from a screenshot of bobjohnsonautogroup.com supplied by the client. The site itself is blocked by this environment's network egress proxy, so hex values were read off the image rather than the stylesheet. They are close; confirm against the real brand sheet.

dealer.name: Bob Johnson
dealer.legalName: Bob Johnson Dodge Jeep Ram of Watertown
dealer.storeNote: Rooftop is the Watertown store. Its own page heading reads BOB JOHNSON DODGE JEEP RAM, so that is what the emails print, though the group site also lists it as Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram and the page shows Chrysler among available makes. Say the word if it should read Chrysler. State stays NY, so the ORIAS obligor in the footer is still correct.

color.$note: Black and gold, read from the wordmark and the primary buttons on the live site. accentDark is a darkened gold used only for small caps labels, because gold at 9px on white does not carry enough contrast to read.

logo.$note: useImage is false, so the header renders a hand built type lockup rather than the hosted PNG: heavy black italic wordmark, a two segment gold rule, and AUTO GROUP letterspaced beneath. The hosted file could not be inspected from the build environment and rendered badly, and a lockup we control also survives the images-off case, which is a large share of email opens. Set useImage true once a file has been checked at the width below.

wordmark.$note: The rule colour is always color.accent. It is not set here, so the two can never drift apart.

contact.addressNote: CONFIRMED from the dealership page: 18712 US-11, Watertown, NY 13601.
contact.phoneNote: CONFIRMED from the dealership page. Sales, service and parts all use this number.
contact.replyToNote: Replies go back to the sending mailbox, which is monitored by the dealer. Workflow 06 reads that same mailbox over IMAP and is careful to ignore ordinary replies so a customer asking a question is never suppressed.

campaign.quoteUrlNote: Two shapes are supported, set by linkMode. "short" builds SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL + "/" + quote_short_links.short_code, e.g. .../KwR8HW4m. "uuid" builds SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL + "/" + the quote id. Only the customer facing base is missing. Note /api/partners/quotes/<uuid> is the partner API, key protected, so it is not what a customer can click.
campaign.unsubscribeNote: Supabase Edge Function vsc-unsubscribe, already deployed. Public by design: the audience is a car owner clicking a link in an email and has no session. Authorisation is the opaque per recipient key in the URL. A GET only renders the page and the opt out is a POST, so mail scanners following links cannot unsubscribe anyone by accident. Set both UNSUBSCRIBE_URL_BASE and PREFERENCES_URL_BASE to this.
campaign.idNote: DO NOT CHANGE. 150 live vsc_enrollment rows and 10 vsc_email_template rows already carry this value, and the scheduler filters on it. Changing it orphans the campaign.

metricbridge.$comment: Dealer identity in MetricBridge. The n8n intake uses these to scope the feed to this rooftop.
metricbridge.program_contact_note: This is the partner contact on the dealer record, not a customer facing service line. The footer uses the public service number instead.
metricbridge.down_payment_note: Confirms the 5% down figure used in emails 1 and 5, straight from the system of record.

supabase.$comment: Supabase is the system of record for service drive capture and for enrollment state. partners.id here equals dealers.source_id in MetricBridge.
supabase.initial_cohort_note: Freshest visits first, capped. The daily send cap does not make this a drip: the backlog all falls due for email 1 at once and the cap just chops that into consecutive days at the ceiling. Total sends are cohort x 10 however slowly you enrol, so capping the cohort is the only lever that actually lowers volume. 150 x 10 over about nine weeks of Tue/Wed/Thu is roughly 52 a send day against a 200 ceiling. Raise it once bounce and complaint rates on the first cohort are clean.
supabase.intake_window_note: Quotes for this rooftop run Feb to Sep 2026: 107 in the last 30 days, 458 within 90. A 30 day window would enroll only the newest 107 and strand the rest, so the backfill runs at 90.
supabase.max_mileage_note: Effectively off. The rating API is keyed on VIN and decides what it can rate, so a local ceiling would only second guess it. A vehicle it cannot price records a pricing_error, is never sent, and stops being retried after five attempts. Removing the ceiling took the list from 269 to 432.
supabase.slug_note: partners.slug in Supabase and dealers.slug in MetricBridge agree. Short codes are globally unique across all 2,199 links, so the slug is probably a partner portal path rather than part of the quote link. If the link does carry it, put it in SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL and nothing in the workflow changes.

brandLead.$comment: dealer means the dealership colour leads the layout and DriveOne cyan is reduced to the provider mark in the header. Set to driveone to flip it back.

sending.$comment: Throughput and timing. These are starting heuristics, not measured truths. Supabase already stores last_email_opened_at and email_open_count, so tune days and hours against real opens once a few thousand sends have landed.
sending.dailyCapNote: Hard ceiling per calendar day in dealer local time, enforced inside the atomic claim so two scheduler runs cannot jointly exceed it.
sending.daysNote: Tuesday through Friday. Monday is excluded because Monday inboxes are cleared in bulk. Friday is INCLUDED for an arithmetic reason, not a preference: two days drawn from Tue/Wed/Thu alone can only ever be 1, 2, 5, 6 or 7 days apart, so a 3 or 4 day cadence gap is impossible to express and the deck opens with both. On the old window every gap silently became 7 days and the 60 day campaign became a flat 64 day weekly drip. Widening to Friday makes every gap in campaign.json achievable. If this is ever narrowed again, re-run n8n/verify.mjs: the cadence check is what catches it.
sending.hoursNote: Local. Mid morning and early afternoon, skipping the lunch hour. Sends are spread evenly across the remaining hours rather than fired in one burst at the top of the window, which is both better for engagement and much gentler on a warmed domain.
sending.maxPerRunNote: Ceiling on any single hourly run, so a backlog cannot arrive as one spike.
